item.title: STAFF POST OPEN - Crosslink Proposal
item.content:encoded:
The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team.

Show Reasoning
Hide Reasoning

The following Crosslink Proposal is being made due to the "pocket dimension" described as being contained within 911's similarities to SCP-3001.

Editing this:

The next thing I knew, I was floating in an endless void.

To this:

The next thing I knew, I was floating in an endless void.1

Footnotes
1. Further descriptions by 914-4 of this "void" are comparably similar to descriptions of SCP-3001 recorded by Dr. Scranton. Investigation into possible links between the two anomalies are ongoing.

EDIT: The "First One", maybe?

item.content:encoded: There is nothing that I can say about this that hasn't already been said, save for the fact that I enjoy the professor. Maybe I'm reading my own experience with solitary confinement into this, but he sounds shaken. The point where he's functional and sane, but his time in isolation did take its toll. I'd say 'wound' but that seems a bit melodramatic.

item.content:encoded:
Hmm. I didn't see or even read about "Hereafter." Probably both use a fairly classic version of Limbo.

You have a point about the description. "Inside the book" could be metaphorical for some unknown space that the scroll is a gateway into.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Thanks! Yeah, I can see how the title could lead to something bad…

In storytelling terms, I wanted to give folks a taste of the kind of people one gets back from the object, and get on to the interview.

In-universe, there is the argument that it wastes a lot of D-class to get back a few people who are not really all that useful to the Foundation.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
For instance, it could be inferred, but how does the Foundation "know" that the consciousness has been transferred into the book? Can they see it?

I'd think that they gained this information through interviews with the subjects that escaped from the papyrus; both 911-2 and 911-4, for instance, were able to describe how things looked "inside" the scroll.
